instruction: Riga 14: l'abstract e' identico parola per parola allo short paper (9 frasi su 9, 246 parole) e la regola CIBB chiede un abstract diverso; limite LNCS 150-250 parole. Riscriverlo intorno all'estensione (nuovo riferimento CPU spatial di S1, D-01; difetto della co-occorrenza GPU, D-13) recependo le voci di frase R0007, R0565, R0566, R0567, R0240, R0568, R0254, R0711, R0639 e i vincoli D-02 e D-04 (44x come confronto di tempi). We compared rapids-singlecell on NVIDIA H100 GPUs with Scanpy on 100 logical CPUs of a DGX H100 cluster, on 10,000 to 1.3 million mouse brain cells sampled from CELLxGENE Census, with five repeats per configuration. At 1.3 million cells the GPU pipeline took 435 s against 52,056 s on CPU (119.6-fold; 105.5-fold in a run that differed only in data loading). Wilcoxon differential expression accounted for 93.5% of the CPU time; without it the speedup was 7.9-9.2-fold. In the multi-GPU configuration tested, additional GPUs did not take part in the computation. At 10,000 cells HVG selection was identical and Leiden clustering agreed with ARI 0.908-0.963. A memory-optimised pipeline processed 11.9 million cells, built from copies of a 3,436,470-cell dataset, on one node, limited by host RAM. Pseudo-bulk differential expression finished 44 times sooner than the cell-level t-test at 3.4 million cells. For spatial data we rebuilt the CPU reference with one fresh process per repeat and the same cell groups for CPU and GPU. Against this DGX CPU reference, an RTX 4090 accelerated end-to-end analysis 1.4-fold on Visium v1, 6.9-fold on Visium HD 8 um (without co-occurrence) and 10.4-fold on Visium HD 2 um. At Visium HD 8 um, GPU co-occurrence in rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 was wrong at 41 of 49 distances because of 32-bit integer overflow; version 0.15.1 matched the CPU at all 49 distances in the same time."
